detailed_rationale:
RVNL is India's dedicated railway-infrastructure EPC arm under the Ministry of Railways, executing new lines, doubling, electrification, metro and increasingly non-rail diversification work such as the ~Rs 13,236 cr BharatNet telecom-infrastructure programme, alongside flagship rail jobs like the Rs 37,000 cr Rishikesh-Karnaprayag line. The order book stood at roughly Rs 99,262 cr entering FY27 (~5x FY26 revenue of Rs 20,412 cr), giving genuine multi-year revenue visibility, and management guides 15-20% FY27 revenue growth off this backlog plus a stated shift toward 'selective, margin-focused bidding.' On the surface this reads as a strong-growth PSU infra compounder riding the national rail-capex cycle.

The problem is what that growth has been earning. FY26 net profit fell ~32% YoY (Rs 871 cr vs Rs 1,282 cr) even as revenue was roughly flat, EPS dropping from Rs 6.15 to Rs 4.20, and quarterly operating margins have swung violently -- 7.0% two quarters back down to just 1.4% in the most recent print, a collapse management itself attributed to onerous-contract and JV-reconciliation charges (~Rs 89 cr) plus execution-cost and working-capital strain tied to a stretched ~Rs 3,400 cr Ministry of Railways receivable -- debtor days have extended from 27 to 96 over the past year. Interest coverage is thin at ~1.8x.

Against that profile the stock still trades near 54-55x trailing earnings (ROE ~9-14%, ROCE ~11%) -- a rich multiple for a business whose realized margins and cash conversion are moving the wrong way, even if the order book itself is real. Quality (37/100) and value (21/100) scores in our framework are both weak, consistent with a name whose valuation has outrun its actual returns on capital, and the balance-sheet flag is amber. Until margin recovery and receivable collection actually show up in reported numbers -- not just guidance -- this is a Sell on a hold-review basis.
recommendation_rationale: Sell, matching the quant call -- not rescued. The order book (~5x revenue) de-risks the revenue side of the growth story, but it does not fix the returns-on-capital and cash-conversion deterioration a fund manager should price: FY26 profit fell a third, margins swung down to 1.4% in the latest quarter, and debtor days nearly quadrupled against the Railways receivable. At ~54-55x trailing earnings for high-single-digit ROCE with margins and collections both moving the wrong way, the valuation is not yet validated by the underlying economics, so this does not clear the bar for a rescue to Hold.
summary: RVNL has a very large, multi-year railway and telecom-infrastructure order book (about Rs 99,000 crore, roughly 5x last year's revenue) and sits at the center of India's rail-capex programme, but recent profitability has weakened sharply -- FY26 net profit fell about a third even as revenue was flat, operating margin fell as low as ~1.4% in the latest quarter, and payments from its main government client have slowed markedly (collection days have nearly quadrupled over the year). The stock still trades at a rich ~55x earnings multiple despite this. We see the order-book story as genuine but not yet delivering the returns the valuation assumes, and recommend Sell on a hold-review basis until margin recovery and collections actually show up in the numbers.
positive_para: The bull case is straightforward: RVNL sits at the center of India's railway capital-expenditure programme with an order book of roughly Rs 99,000 crore -- nearly five times FY26 revenue -- spanning new lines, doubling, electrification and a growing non-rail book (the Rs 13,236 crore BharatNet telecom project) that management says carries better margins than legacy rail EPC work. Guidance is for 15-20% revenue growth in FY27, and as a quasi-sovereign-backed contractor whose principal client is also its majority owner, ultimate counterparty credit risk on receivables is low even when collection timing is slow. If the promised shift to 'selective, margin-focused bidding' actually sticks, there is real optionality for margin recovery off a depressed base.
negative_para: The bear case is that the growth story hasn't been translating into economic returns. FY26 net profit fell ~32% YoY on flat revenue, and quarterly operating margin has been extremely volatile -- as low as 1.4% in the most recent quarter (from 7.0% two quarters earlier) -- with management explicitly citing onerous-contract and JV-reconciliation charges plus execution-cost pressure. Cash conversion has deteriorated alongside: debtor days have stretched from 27 to 96 over the past year against a large (~Rs 3,400 crore) Railways receivable, and interest coverage is thin at ~1.8x. None of this is being priced conservatively -- the stock still trades near 54-55x trailing earnings against ROE in the 9-14% range and ROCE of ~11%, a valuation that assumes the margin and cash-conversion problems are temporary. If they persist even one more year, the multiple has real room to compress further, and a large order book does not, by itself, fix a working-capital or margin problem.
reverse_dcf_judgment: At ~54-55x trailing EPS against ROE of roughly 9-14% and ROCE near 11%, the multiple is pricing a meaningfully better-margin, better-cash-conversion version of this business than the one currently reporting -- essentially a bet that the BharatNet-led diversification and the 'margin-focused bidding' shift lift blended EPC margins back toward historical highs (~7-10% operating margin) and that Railways receivables normalize. The order book (~5x revenue) makes the revenue side of that bet low-risk; the margin and cash-conversion side is unproven in the last two quarters' data. Judgment: rich, not cheap -- the current price is paying up front for a recovery that hasn't shown up yet.
